newsitem.title: UK: ICO report sees drop in Indian exportable coffee.
newsitem.headline: ICO report sees drop in Indian exportable coffee.

text.p: India's exportable coffee supply could fall sharply to 2.50 million bags in 1996-97 (October/September) from 3.65 million the previous year, owing to a big drop in stocks, the International Coffee Organization said on Tuesday.
A special ICO report on the Indian coffee sector said production would reach 3.41 million bags in 96-97 compared with 3.72 million in the previous year.
Domestic consumption is about 1.0 million bags. The estimate for the amount of available for export includes exportable production of 2.4 million bags and stocks of 89,000.
In 1995/95 stocks totalled almost one million bags.
The ICO said India produces arabica and robusta coffees in almost equal proportion, although robustas were showing comparitively higher growth in production.
Coffee production was affected by a strong biannual cycle but the underlying trend was moderately positive, the ICO said. Average annual production increased by about 80,000 bags in recent years.
The chairman of the Indian Coffee Board, Philipose Matthai, said the shift towards robusta production is likely to continue. This was because robustas were more resistant to diseases and pests.
He believed that current high prices and an extension of coffee farming into the northweast of India would result in a continued rise in output.
